item.title: OP delivered. Fight me.
item.description: EDITED: Hey guys. I said I'd share the whole thing and here it is. (background at the bottom if you're new!) github.com/812theory/812 All 8 episodes. Every draft. Every background doc. The pitch materials. The coverage that called it unpitchable. The mess I made before I figured out what I was making. It's all there, nothing hidden. I genuinely hope it helps at least one writer who's earlier in their journey than they want to be. That's the whole point. Now... if you thought any of this was AI, go read the mess. Then come fight me. For people who are new: In 2019 I posted a short story to r/HFY called "I Am Not a God." https://www.reddit.com/r/HFY/comments/egluod/i_am_not_a_god_oc/ A man in a bungalow in Bangkok. People bent reality around him without realizing it. He didn't notice because he'd been alive for centuries and his brain had built a wall around everything he couldn't process. No genre, no plan, just a character I couldn't stop thinking about. That post went nowhere. I filed it away. Seven years later I pulled it back out. By then I'd sold scripts to Netflix and worked on Strange New Worlds for 3.5 seasons. I'd also spent three months in an ICU and three months in addiction treatment. Turns out the character had been waiting for me to become the person who could actually write him. In about two weeks it became an 8-episode limited series. Something is eating Bangkok, not destroying it, organizing it. The 7-11 door chime is the first thing that goes. A structural engineer who's been alive for centuries walks the same route every morning at 8:12 AM and genuinely doesn't notice that traffic stops for him. Some of you saw me posting about the process while I was in it. Then I finished it. And I said I'd share the whole thing when I did. So here it is. The show, every draft, every background doc, the pitch bible that got called unpitchable, thirteen production rules, the Reddit post that started everything in 2019, and the thinking behind every choice. Open source. Take it, learn from it, steal the good parts. github.com/812theory/812 EDIT: 4pm EST: I captured five moments from this comment thread that broke something open — about the work, about the audience, about what it even means to open source a TV show. What happened when the work met the world: https://github.com/812theory/812/blob/main/the-making/launch-feedback.md
